name: Number Theory
description: Divisibility, congruences, primes and the group structure of the integers mod n, through to the maths of public-key cryptography.

nodes.name: Divisibility
nodes.desc: Divisors, the division algorithm and proofs about divisibility.
nodes.summary: You will be able to reason about divisors with the division algorithm and write short proofs of divisibility statements.

nodes.name: GCD & Euclid
nodes.desc: Greatest common divisors and Euclid's algorithm with its running time.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compute greatest common divisors with Euclid's algorithm and explain why it runs in logarithmic time.
topics: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a mod b)

nodes.name: Extended Euclid
nodes.desc: Bezout's identity and computing its coefficients.
nodes.summary: You will be able to prove Bezout's identity and compute integer coefficients x and y with the extended Euclidean algorithm.

nodes.name: Primes
nodes.desc: Prime numbers, the infinitude of primes and unique factorisation.
nodes.summary: You will be able to prove there are infinitely many primes and use unique prime factorisation to reason about integers.
topics: Euclid's proof of infinitely many primes

nodes.name: Modular arithmetic
nodes.desc: Congruence classes and adding, multiplying and reducing mod n.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compute with congruences, reducing sums, products and powers modulo n correctly.

nodes.name: Modular inverses
nodes.desc: When inverses exist and computing them with extended Euclid.
nodes.summary: You will be able to decide when an integer has an inverse modulo n and compute it with the extended Euclidean algorithm.

nodes.name: Linear congruences
nodes.desc: Solving ax = b (mod n) and counting solutions.
nodes.summary: You will be able to solve linear congruences ax ≡ b (mod n) and count how many solutions exist.
topics: Solvability condition gcd(a, n) divides b
Reducing the congruence by the gcd

nodes.name: Chinese remainder
nodes.desc: The Chinese remainder theorem and solving systems of congruences.
nodes.summary: You will be able to solve systems of congruences with the Chinese remainder theorem, including moduli that are not pairwise coprime.
topics: Statement of the Chinese remainder theorem
Using CRT to speed up computations

nodes.name: Fast exponentiation
nodes.desc: Square-and-multiply for computing large powers mod n.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compute large modular powers efficiently with square-and-multiply in logarithmically many steps.

nodes.name: Sieves
nodes.desc: Sieve of Eratosthenes, linear sieve and segmented sieves.
nodes.summary: You will be able to generate primes up to a bound with the sieve of Eratosthenes, a linear sieve and a segmented sieve.
topics: Linear sieve with smallest prime factors

nodes.name: Fermat & Euler
nodes.desc: Euler's totient, Fermat's little theorem and Euler's theorem.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compute Euler's totient and apply Fermat's little theorem and Euler's theorem to modular powers.

nodes.name: Primality testing
nodes.desc: Fermat and Miller-Rabin tests and why randomness helps.
nodes.summary: You will be able to test large numbers for primality with Fermat and Miller-Rabin tests and explain their error probabilities.

nodes.name: Factorisation
nodes.desc: Trial division, Pollard's rho and why factoring is believed hard.
nodes.summary: You will be able to factor integers with trial division and Pollard's rho and explain why factoring large numbers is believed hard.
topics: Trial division up to the square root

nodes.name: Prime distribution
nodes.desc: The prime number theorem and gaps between primes.
nodes.summary: You will understand how primes are distributed through the prime number theorem and known results about gaps between primes.

nodes.name: NT library
nodes.desc: Write a tested number theory library: gcd, inverses, CRT, sieves and primality.
nodes.summary: You will write a tested number theory library covering gcd, modular inverses, CRT, sieves and primality tests.
topics: API design for number theory routines

nodes.name: Groups mod n
nodes.desc: The multiplicative group of integers mod n and element orders.
nodes.summary: You will be able to describe the multiplicative group of integers mod n and compute the order of its elements.
topics: The group of units mod n

nodes.name: Primitive roots
nodes.desc: Generators of cyclic groups and when primitive roots exist.
nodes.summary: You will be able to find primitive roots, test candidates efficiently and state for which moduli they exist.
topics: Testing candidates with prime factors of phi

nodes.name: Quadratic residues
nodes.desc: Squares mod p, the Legendre symbol and quadratic reciprocity.
nodes.summary: You will be able to determine which numbers are squares modulo a prime using the Legendre symbol and quadratic reciprocity.

nodes.name: Discrete logarithm
nodes.desc: The discrete log problem and baby-step giant-step.
nodes.summary: You will understand the discrete logarithm problem and be able to solve small instances with baby-step giant-step.

nodes.name: RSA mathematics
nodes.desc: Why RSA works, key generation and the role of factoring.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain why RSA decryption works, generate keys and relate RSA's security to integer factorisation.
topics: Key generation with primes p and q

nodes.name: Diffie-Hellman
nodes.desc: Key exchange from the hardness of discrete logarithms.
nodes.summary: You will be able to carry out Diffie-Hellman key exchange and explain how its security rests on the discrete logarithm problem.

nodes.name: Elliptic curves
nodes.desc: The group law on elliptic curves over finite fields.
nodes.summary: You will be able to perform point addition on elliptic curves over finite fields and see why they support smaller cryptographic keys.

nodes.name: Toy RSA & DH
nodes.desc: Implement textbook RSA and Diffie-Hellman and attack weak parameter choices.
nodes.summary: You will implement textbook RSA and Diffie-Hellman and break them when parameters are chosen badly.
topics: Common modulus and shared factor attacks
